one_liner: Hand-written ARMv6-M assembly float/double library for Cortex-M0, 1.3-14x fewer cycles than GCC's soft-float and math routines.
what_it_does: Mark Owen's Qfplib-M0-full, packaged for RT-Thread: one GNU assembler file plus a C header that provide IEEE single- and double-precision add, sub, mul, div, sqrt, compare, sin, cos, tan, atan2, exp, ln and a full set of int/fixed-point/float/double conversions for FPU-less Cortex-M0/M0+ parts. It is not a transparent replacement: you call qfp_fadd, qfp_dsin and so on explicitly, and the compiler's own float operators keep calling libgcc.
how_it_is_fast: Every routine is hand-scheduled Thumb-1 code that works on unpacked two's-complement mantissas in registers, with no static storage and no recursion. Add, sub, mul, div and sqrt are correctly rounded integer-mantissa routines. The scientific functions use CORDIC-style shift-and-add iterations in fixed point (rotation mode for sin/cos with the remaining iterations collapsed into one multiplication, vector mode for atan2, table-driven x += x>>i steps for exp, tan as sin/cos plus one divide), so each call is a short integer sequence instead of a chain of generic soft-float operations. Double sin/cos reduce the argument to a residual below 2^-32 in Q62 plus Q62 cos/sin of the reduced angle.
when_to_use: FPU-less Cortex-M0/M0+ firmware whose hot loop does float division or square roots: qfp_fdiv 83 vs 475 cycles and qfp_fsqrt 67 vs 460 for the GCC library.
Scientific functions on an M0 with bounded arguments (|x| up to 128 for single, 1024 for double) where about 1 ulp suffices: qfp_fsin 584 vs 3300 cycles, qfp_fln 277 vs 3960.
Double precision on an M0 without paying for it: every Qfplib double routine is faster than GCC's single-precision one (qfp_dmul 163 vs GCC fmul 166).
Flash- and RAM-tight or certification-minded projects: under 6 KB of code, no static data, statically analysable stack use.
GPLv2-compatible RT-Thread projects built with GCC, where enabling the package is a menuconfig switch.
when_not_to_use: Proprietary firmware that cannot carry GPLv2-only code (the README says to ask the author for other licensing).
Code that relies on IEEE special values: NaNs become infinities and denormals are flushed to zero, so isnan() checks and gradual underflow break.

Trigonometry on large or very small arguments: single-precision sin/cos/tan need |x| below 128 (double below 1024), and the fixed-point reduction gives absolute rather than relative accuracy near multiples of pi, including near zero.
Cortex-M3/M4/M7: the README says it runs there but is not optimised; use the hardware FPU or a library tuned for ARMv7-M.
Keil (armcc) or IAR builds: only the GCC assembler source is in the repo; on RP2040 use the pico-sdk float routines, which call the same author's code in ROM.

integration.min_toolchain: GNU assembler from arm-none-eabi-gcc (unified Thumb syntax, .cpu cortex-m0plus); RT-Thread SCons for the package build; compiler version used for the README numbers not documented
integration.platforms: ARMv6-M Cortex-M0/M0+ (soft-float calling convention); the README says it also runs, unoptimised, on Cortex-M3 and M4
integration.thread_safety: reentrant by design: the README states no static storage and no recursion, with statically analysable stack use
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — functionally equivalent for non-exceptional arguments, but you must call qfp_* explicitly; no __aeabi_* or libm aliases are exported, so a + b and sinf() in C still go to libgcc and libm

gotchas: Single-precision trig is fixed point with absolute, not relative, error: qfp_fsin calls qfp_float2fix(x, 24), which truncates the argument toward minus infinity to Q24 and clamps on overflow, then reduces it by repeated subtraction of a Q24 2*pi and runs a Q29 CORDIC (with a '+9 fiddle factor to make sin(0)==0'). By code reading (not run), arguments below 2^-24 return 0, x = 1e-6 is evaluated as 16*2^-24 = 9.54e-7 (about 4.6% low), and |x| of 128 or more is silently clamped instead of flagged. This is the README's 'poorer near a multiple of pi' caveat, quantified, and part of why it beats a full-range sinf.

Calling convention: the header declares plain float/double prototypes and the assembly reads its arguments from r0-r3 (qfp_fadd unpacks r0 and r1). On an FPU core built with -mfloat-abi=hard the compiler passes floats in FPU registers, so the README's 'runs on Cortex-M4' only holds with the soft or softfp ABI.

The RT-Thread SConscript adds *_rvds.S for armcc and *_iar.S for IAR, but only qfplib-m0-full_gcc.S exists, so a Keil or IAR build compiles nothing from the package and every qfp_* call fails at link time.

The speed table is the upstream author's approximate averages, including call overhead, for non-exceptional arguments on an LPC11U68 (Cortex-M0+) running from single-cycle flash. The GCC version, flags and math library are not stated, the argument distribution for the scientific functions is not given (the sin/cos range-reduction loop grows with |x|), no harness is in the repo, and the 'GoFast' column is inferred from an ARM7TDMI page; GoFast beats Qfplib on fsin, fcos, dsin and dcos.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The pico-sdk entry's RP2040 float routines are the same author's code: the RP2040 bootrom's mufplib.S (Copyright 2020 Mark Owen, licensed for RP2040 use only, also available under GPLv2) has the identical Q24 CORDIC sin/cos path. Pick Qfplib-M0-full for other Cortex-M0/M0+ parts (non-RP2040) where GPLv2 is acceptable; on an RP2040 use the SDK. rt_memcpy_cm from the same RT-Thread packager covers memcpy, not floating point.
verified_claims_summary: The README table gives approximate average cycle counts, including calling overhead, for non-exceptional arguments on an NXP LPC11U68 (Cortex-M0+, single-cycle flash) against an unversioned 'GCC library' (libgcc soft-float, plus presumably newlib libm for the scientific functions): fadd 76 vs 102 (1.34x), fmul 62 vs 166 (2.7x), fdiv 83 vs 475 (5.7x), fsqrt 67 vs 460 (6.9x), fsin 584 vs 3300 (5.7x), fln 277 vs 3960 (14.3x), dmul 163 vs 377 (2.3x), ddiv 200 vs 1190 (6.0x), dln 464 vs 4375 (9.4x) (ratios derived from page data). No compiler version, flags or harness are given.
status_note: An RT-Thread packaging (4 commits, last 2021-05-26, no issues) of Mark Owen's 2019-2020 Qfplib, abandoned as a package but small enough to vendor (one .S file under 6 KB) and GPLv2-only; upstream quinapalus.com did not resolve from this session, so newer upstream releases or fixes were not checked.
